newsitem.title: USA: Cyrix jumps on better-than-expected net.
newsitem.headline: Cyrix jumps on better-than-expected net.

text.p: Cyrix Corp's share price jumped as much as 28 percent Thursday morning after the computer chip maker reported first-quarter net income that far surpassed Wall Street expectations.
Cyrix, which make microprocessors to run personal computers, also said it expects brisk business for its new MediaGX and older 6x86 chips for the rest of the year.
Shares of the Richardson, Texas, company were up 4-1/8 to 21-7/8 on trading of 2.24 million shares. It was among the most active Nasdaq stocks.
"They had a very good quarter," said Kenneth Toudouze, analyst at Principal Financial Securities in Dallas.

He said Cyrix had much-better-than-expected gross margins -- a measure of how much profit is made on each dollar of product sold -- which showed the company has improved its manufacturing efficiency, Toudouze said.
After the market closed yesterday, Cyrix said its first-quarter net income had more than tripled, to $6.6 million, or $0.33 a share, from the year-earlier $2 million, or $0.10 a share.
Wall Street had expected Cyrix to earn $0.09 a share, according to a recent survey of analysts by Zacks Investment Research.
First-quarter revenues rose 47 percent, to $75.6 million from $51.6 million a year earlier.

Cyrix makes microprocessors that mimick the way Pentium chips from Intel Corp work. Earlier this year Cyrix introduced its MediaGX chip, which works about as fast as Intel's mid-range Pentiums but is much less expensive.

Compaq Computer Corp, the world's biggest PC maker, is a MediaGX customer. It uses the chips in machines that retail for less than $1,000, a product category that analysts expect to be the hottest this year.
"Stronger-than-planned unit shipments at the end of the (first) quarter helped us to exceed our profit goals," said Jay Swent, Cyrix chief financial officer and acting chief executive.
Cyrix plans to introduce its M2 chip -- a rival to Intel's top-of-the-line Pentium Pro -- in June, Swent said. Production of the new chip should be in full swing by the third quarter.
